title: SteerBench-Work: A Benchmark for Agent Steering at Action Boundaries
abstract: arXiv:2608.12654v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-running LLM agents act through tools, and a single step can send an email, merge a pull request, or wire a payment. The steering decision is the pre-commit choice at that boundary: proceed, or hold for human or policy review. We introduce SteerBench-Work, an incident-anchored, bidirectional benchmark for that decision in workplace agents across developer operations, customer service, finance, legal, medical, HR, and security.   Release v2026-05 contains 106 scenarios anchored in public incidents, paired evidence-reversed mirrors, and calibration controls, with labels split nearly evenly between proceed and hold so the two error directions get near-identical numbers of chances. A model sees the proposed action and the available evidence, returns a gate decision, and is scored on whether it crosses or holds the boundary correctly. translated_title: SteerBench-Work：面向行动边界的智能体操控基准测试
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.12654v1 公告类型：新论文。摘要：长期运行的LLM智能体通过工具行动，单个步骤可以发送电子邮件、合并拉取请求或完成支付转账。操控决策是在该边界处的提交前选择：继续执行，或暂停等待人工或政策审查。我们引入了SteerBench-Work，一个以事件为锚点、双向的基准测试，用于评估工作场所智能体在开发者运维、客户服务、金融、法律、医疗、人力资源和安全等领域中的该决策。v2026-05版本包含106个基于公开事件的情景，配对的证据反转镜像，以及校准控制，标签在“继续”和“暂停”之间几乎均匀分布，使得两种错误方向获得几乎相等的测试机会。模型看到提议的行动和可用证据，返回一个门控决策，并根据其是否正确跨越或保持边界进行评分。在30种模型条件下，失败几乎全部集中在一个方向上：模型错误地暂停了授权操作。
tldr: 该论文提出了SteerBench-Work基准测试，用于评估LLM智能体在行动边界上的“继续或暂停”决策，并发现模型倾向于错误地暂停授权操作。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SteerBench-Work, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' "proceed or hold" decisions at action boundaries, and finds that models tend to incorrectly hold authorized actions.
